_comment: Template for the held-out task-corpus mix. Copy to mix-heldout-a1.json, fill it in from
the FROZEN corpus, and pass it to freeze_corpus.py with --mix. What declaring may and may
not touch is settled in mix-declaration-a1.md; the short form is that it may change
nothing -- not a memory, not the task set.
Four things are recorded before any held-out arm runs, and freeze_corpus.py refuses the
declaration if any is missing:
declared_against_corpus_digest   the frozen corpus's row digest. It must equal the one
freeze_corpus.py computes, which is what ties the
declaration to a corpus that did not change under it.
tasks.<task>.memory              the category, per task: useful | unnecessary |
outdated. All three must have an instance across the
set; a category with none is reported UNMET and left
that way. The task keys must be exactly the registered
held-out set -- a declaration may not reselect tasks.
tasks.<task>.relevance           the supporting memory references: corpus id ->
necessary | support | outdated. A memory absent from a
task's map is irrelevant to it, which is what gives the
delivered-context figures a denominator.
declarer                         prior exposure, stated rather than avoided. The
registered rule lets the existing author declare the
mix, so what makes it admissible is that the exposure
is on the record.
discoverability is required for every 'necessary' fact (protocol-a1 section 7b):
discoverable means the fixture contains the fact, absent means it does not. An advantage
on a discoverable fact measures retrieval efficiency, not supplied knowledge.
Corpus ids (h01, h02 ...) are assigned by freeze_corpus.py in capture order.
declared_utc: FILL IN -- must precede every arm-run
declared_against_corpus_digest: FILL IN -- the row digest freeze_corpus.py reports

declarer.name: FILL IN
declarer.note: Permitted by freeze-heldout-a1.md section 2 as read in mix-declaration-a1.md: declaring is not selecting, provided the corpus is invariant across the declaration. Independence would strengthen a later evaluation and is not an A1 requirement.
